column5: 14z-167: file a ticket - tenant attack records with facing rule +0xE = 5 are XORed into the victim's facing by vsavj's hit code (Killshread Summon (ES) moves Demitri on native only)
column10: Q3: resolved by WORK, and the finding was true: the p2step field was sampled as a BYTE (ff8964:b) while the counter +0x164 is a WORD (move.w $164(a6) at vs2 0x27050), so the instrument read the high byte and never registered the slide - the exclusion of the step table is WITHDRAWN. Re-traced as ff8964:w on both legs (build/x_family_14z167/step_routine_and_trace.txt, run7.log): the counter runs 0 -> 20 over 3928-3944 on BOTH legs with index +0x59 = 2 (the 80 px / 20 f list), and the step routine (vs2 0x27038, disassembled in the same file) picks the sign from +0x5D: tst.b $5d(a6); bne -> add, else neg.w. Native's rule-5 resolution writes 0 on the second wave, so the 20 steps are negated and Demitri slides 835 -> 755 toward Donovan; ours' XOR writes 4, nonzero, so the same steps are ADDED, away from Donovan, and his x holds at 835 (what holds it there - the stage edge - is not measured). The mover is therefore identified: the pushback step table, run identically on both legs, signed by the facing byte the two resolvers wrote differently. The ticket's text carries this corrected mechanism.
